title: AI calls
grade_reasons: C, in its lower half; the steward's grade holds against the verified findings. The base is sound and partly held: the shopper chat sends about 5,100 characters a call, the other agents are small, search answers are kept, tools of switched-off features are dropped, and a turn has ceilings of time and tokens. But the dearest call, the AI manager's, sends 161,661 characters on every round (3.3 times a lean round, up to 11 times a turn), nothing counts cached or output tokens, the only size budget is a tool count set at the provider's cap, and four upkeep jobs and 12.4 connection reads per AI call run with no model called. It is not a D because the waste sits in one agent and follows use, and not an E because nobody is hurt and the money is cents while only the team uses it.
verdict_on_bar: FLOOR CHECKED. I ran the planners' bundle of the app's own functions again: the floor is 33,198 characters (prompt 14,772, the 12 core tools with load_tools 13,482, the manager's 9 own tools 4,944). The chat chunk is 496,206 bytes, the eval has 9 manager cases and none finds a tool, and src holds no cache marker. KEPT: the cached share (50% in all, 80% after a turn's first round), 2 connection reads per AI call, all 8 small jobs on a quick model, a baseline for every agent. TIGHTENED. (1) The round. The steward's 50,000 and 70,000 are for a round drawn with no question. But the lean round of step 2.36 also sends the area a router picks from the question, and on the planners' own 20 questions that doubles the first round's tools (66,168 characters against 33,009). The bar now covers any first round, question included. (2) The 17 plan, reminder and skill tools are 15,384 characters, a third of a lean round with no page. That is not a small tolerance. The bar is written with them loaded on demand (34,000 and 56,000) and gives the figures if the owner keeps them (48,000 and 70,000; the steward had 50,000). (3) The chat script: 130,000 bytes, the plan's own figure, not 140,000; the sum gives 125,143. (4) Lean eval cases: 12, not 8. Page groups add a new way to fail: the model sees some of an area's tools and stops looking. (5) A small job moves to the quick model only if it passes fixed cases of its own; 5 of the 8 have none today. (6) The listings' check joins the upkeep jobs: it can waste model calls, not only statements. LOOSENED: the median turn from 40,000 to 45,000 tokens, because three calls at the call bar of 15,000 are 45,000. DROPPED: 'under 300 reads on a day with no AI call', a number for today's traffic; the upkeep test holds the idle part (an idle run reads no connection). ADDED: output tokens. An output token costs 8 times an input token at the seeded price (2.00 against 0.25 dollars a million), the two tool loops set no reasoning effort, and after the lean round and the cache, output can be a third to a half of a turn's cost. The steward showed it but set no bar. Also added: a scanned list of public paths that can reach a model, and a daily flag, so a production figure cannot slip unseen. NOT MEASURABLE AS WRITTEN: the median turn and the cached share after a turn's first round (commerce.ai_usage has no turn or round, and the round log is a log line nobody keeps); any figure read with feature = 'ai_manager' alone, because rounds after a report tool are filed under analytics_question (src/server/owner-assistant.ts:824); and the cached figure that step 1.19 shows, whose column step 2.38 adds a phase later.

measures.name: Work done when no model is called: reads of the AI connection, and the five upkeep jobs

Knowledge, product vectors, picture vectors and alt texts walk every site every five minutes: 91,200 deletes removed 782 rows, 10,201 hashes of every product's text, and a failed picture is retried daily with no end. The listings' check can ask a model again every five minutes for an answer it could not read: up to 2,880 calls a day, not measured.

A failed picture is tried at most 5 times. No listing is asked twice in a day for the same words.

bar_in_a_sentence: The AI manager's first round is a third of today's size or less (at most 56,000 characters, and a median of 15,000 real tokens a call), at least half of its input comes from the provider's cache, and an eval shows it still finds its tools. Small jobs run on a small model, nothing reads the AI connection or walks the stores when no model is called, and a test or a daily figure holds every agent's size, output and ceiling.
can_the_steps_reach_a: No, not as written. The steps reach a B at the end of phase 2. Six additions, all small, make it an A there, once a week of production figures is read. THE SUMS. Round: 161,661 today. Step 2.36: the scan's draw falls to 48,582 with no page and 77,014 on orders. Step 2.37: bounds take 4,006 to 7,654 and four areas get page groups, so the draw is 44,576 with no page and under 70,000 on every page drawn but orders. Orders is not grouped and reads 71,452 (about 73,800 with every feature on): over by 1,450 to 3,800. The question: the router adds a whole area, so a shipping question asked from an orders page still sends about 120,000 characters, and the scan draws no question. On the planners' 20 questions a turn costs more tool characters with the router (253,048) than without it (235,761). Tokens: with groups for the routed part too, a first round is 57,000 to 70,000 characters with the 17 tools kept (14,250 to 17,500 tokens at 4 characters a token, before history and tool results) and 43,000 to 56,000 with them on demand (10,700 to 14,000). So a median call of 15,000 holds only with the 17 on demand. Cache (step 2.38): a three-call turn that starts cold is 64% cached, and 93% after its first round. With a load_tools round in 35% of turns it is 79% to 84% after the first, so 80% holds at the edge, and only if loaded tools are added after the fixed block. Reads (steps 0.21, 0.27, 0.28): 12.4 falls toward 1 once the jobs go idle and screens stop asking. The statistics cannot split it, so step 4.5 reads it. Script (step 0.11): 496,206 less 437,753 plus 66,690 is 125,143, under 130,000. Small jobs (step 2.39): 8 of 8 by its scan, but its production check names 3 of the 8. WHERE IT STOPS SHORT: routed rounds and the orders page (shortfall 1); turns and rounds cannot be read, and the cached column comes a phase late (2); output has no bar (3); five small jobs have no cases (4); no list of public paths (5); seven done-whens are weaker than the bar (6). Step 4.5 reads every measure again, but it cannot read what is not drawn or stored.

shortfalls.what: The largest rounds are in no baseline. Step 2.36 sends the page's area and the area a router picks from the question. Step 2.37 then groups only the page's tools, in four areas, and the scan of step 1.19 draws no question. So the scan can pass at 70,000 while a real first round is about 120,000: on the planners' 20 questions the mean first round is 66,168 characters of tools, twice the 33,009 of a round with no question. Orders (25 tools, 28,460 characters) is not among the four areas and misses step 2.37's own done-when by 1,450 to 3,800.

shortfalls.what: Output has no bar. Step 1.19 shows output tokens and tries low reasoning effort once, but sets no number and nothing to keep. At the seeded price an output token costs 8 times an input token. A lean turn of three calls costs about 0.4 cents of input for its first call and little for the cached rest, against up to 0.7 cents of output at the limits (3 x 1,200 tokens at 2.00 dollars a million). So after phase 2 output is the larger unknown. The two tool loops send no reasoning effort; single calls in 11 files ask for low.

The eval run tries low effort on both tool loops and keeps it for an agent only if every case passes. After the first week of real figures, a ceiling per feature is set at that week's 90th percentile plus 20% and joins the daily flag.

shortfalls.what: Step 2.39 moves 8 small jobs to a quick model, but only 3 have fixed cases to judge it by: search understanding (src/lib/query-eval.ts), recommendations (recommend-eval.ts) and the listings' check (in the agents' eval). Tone, the support summary, the memory pass, category suggestion and highlight words have none. The listings' check is a legal duty, so a weaker model there is a risk, not a saving. The step's production check names 3 of the 8 features. A quick model with no price row counts nothing toward a store's allowance.

shortfalls.what: Seven done-whens are weaker than the bar. 0.27 and 0.28 disagree: 0.27 builds one small read per site, and 0.28's proof asks for the same statements with 1 site and 20. 0.28 also does not prove 'at most 8 statements', 'no AI connection read', 'five tries' or 'the product scan hourly', and it counts statements a phase before step 1.9 makes the counter. 1.19 asks for 8 lean cases, not 12, and proves that output is shown, not the input figures. 2.36's 'at most 40 store tools when no area is asked' holds nothing (a lean round sends 12), and it dropped the checks of three findings it closes: no embedding request before the first model call (AI-9), the shorter prompt for a website and for an autopilot step (AI-11), and the turn's new ceiling. It does not record the owner's answer on the 17 tools. 2.37 names four areas, which misses its own figure on orders. 2.38's query is the wrong one (shortfall 2) and it does not prove the reminder still gets the right time once the time moves in the prompt. 2.39 checks 3 of 8 features.

shortfalls.proposed_step_what: No new work, only stronger proofs, in steps 0.27, 0.28, 1.19, 2.36, 2.37, 2.38 and 2.39. In 0.27 the question 'which sites have work' is one statement over all sites. In 0.28 the test uses its own small statement counter until step 1.9 lands.
shortfalls.proposed_done_when: 0.28: an idle run of the five jobs sends at most 8 statements with 1 site and with 20, makes 0 reads of commerce.ai_providers and 0 model calls, a picture with five failed tries is not picked, and in production the product hash statement gains about 24 calls a day (about 130 today). 1.19: 12 lean cases, and the panel shows input per call. 2.36: 12 store tools when no area is asked; 0 embedding requests for a turn of a person with 3 memories; a website's prompt at least 2,500 characters shorter and an autopilot step's prompt without the admin map; TURN_TOKENS_MAX at most 250,000 with its sum in the comment; the owner's answer in docs/decisions.md. 2.38: the query of shortfall 2 gives 0.5 and 0.8, an eval case that asks for a reminder 'tomorrow at 9' sends the right time, and limits-enforce.int.test.ts counts a month with cached tokens as costing less.

tolerated: The 12 core tools go with every round (12,700 characters), also on a turn that uses none. They answer most questions without a second round.
The tools of the page in view and of one group matched to the question are sent before the model asks: up to about 11,500 characters each.
The prompt carries an index of playbooks and the admin map, about 8,000 to 11,000 characters a round, so the manager can name a page or load a playbook.
Up to 35% of turns take one more round, a second or two, because the tool was outside what was sent.
The first call of a cold conversation is not cached. A provider with no cache is outside the cache measure.

The chat script keeps a list of 416 page names in two languages, about 53,500 of its 125,000 bytes, so the suggested question needs no call to the server. It loads once a session, and only when the panel is opened.
One read of the AI connection a minute per server instance and store, to know what the AI can do.
A picture the vision model cannot describe is tried up to five times.
Providers that do not report tokens on a streamed answer (Mistral, a custom address) are counted at four characters a token and left out of the token figures.
If the owner keeps them: the 17 plan, reminder and skill tools on every round, 15,400 characters, named in the baseline.
owner_choices: Step 2.36, the 17 plan, reminder and saved-skill tools. (a) Keep all 17 on every round: about 3,850 tokens a call, and the bar reads 48,000 and 70,000 characters and a median call of 19,000 tokens. (b) Load them when the talk turns to them or a plan, goal or reminder is alive, with one line in the prompt so the manager still offers them unprompted: 34,000 and 56,000 characters and a median call of 15,000 tokens. This is the panel's bar. (c) Keep the four that start something (make a plan, set a goal, set a reminder, save a skill: 7,500 characters) and load the 13 that manage what exists: saves 7,900 characters a round. Every tool stays one call away in all three.

Step 2.34: may the notice badge in a tab nobody touches be up to ten minutes late (60 requests an hour become 6)? It shows at once on the next click and stays at one minute while an approval waits. No AI measure moves; it closes the area's last finding.

The eval is run by a person with platform access in production, and its recording committed, at least four times: after steps 1.19, 2.36 with 2.38, 2.37 and 2.39. Each of those steps waits for that run. Who does it?
Step 2.39: the listings' check is a legal duty. Should it stay on the main model whatever the price, or move to the quick model if its cases pass?
